summary: Tam khanun (ตำขนุน), also called tam ba-nun, is a northern Thai savory preparation of boiled young jackfruit pounded and stir-fried with herbs and curry paste. It is often finished with minced pork, tomatoes, kaffir lime, fried garlic and pork crackling; versions vary.
whyGo: A distinctly Lanna way to cook jackfruit: savory, fibrous and aromatic rather than sweet.
Order one plate to share alongside sticky rice and other northern dishes.
bestFor: Curious eaters who want a regional dish beyond khao soi.
People comfortable with chili, fermented seasonings and variable recipes.
skipIf: You need a reliably vegetarian, vegan, pork-free or allergen-controlled dish; the base paste and kitchen handling need checking.
You dislike soft, mashed textures or rich, oily preparations.
duration: Allow about 45–90 minutes for a casual sit-down meal; this is a planning estimate, not a service-time guarantee.
cost: A current Chiang Mai menu at Khoei Chiang Mai lists tam khanun at ฿95, excluding VAT. Allow roughly ฿110–150 for the dish plus rice and tax; menu prices may change before December 2026.
hours: Khoei Chiang Mai's contact page lists daily 09:00–00:00, last order 23:30; it advises checking holiday hours. Confirm in December before going.
bestTime: Lunch or early dinner gives the best chance to find the dish before it sells out; confirm availability when ordering. December does not appear to require a special seasonal date for this dish.
gettingThere: One concrete option is Khoei Chiang Mai, 14 Santitham Road, Chang Phueak, near the Santitham five-way junction and YMCA lane. Use a metered taxi or ride-hailing app from the Old City, or ask a red songthaew driver for Santitham; agree the fare before boarding. Exact journey time and fare depend on starting point and traffic. The restaurant lists parking across the road.
booking: No booking is needed for a single dish, but call +66 93 138 5553 or message the restaurant's LINE account to confirm tam khanun is available and check holiday hours. It accepts table reservations.
accessibility: The venue's site gives an address and parking details but no step-free entrance, accessible toilet or seating information. Contact it ahead if access matters. Specific allergen and cross-contact procedures are also not published.
practicalTips: At Khoei Chiang Mai, ask for ตำขนุน (tam khanun); menu translation: Northern Style Young Jackfruit Salad.
Ask whether that day's version contains minced pork, shrimp paste, fermented fish or soybean paste (ถั่วเน่า), and whether pork crackling is served on top. Recipes differ.
Request mild or less spicy seasoning, but note the kitchen may not be able to adjust a pre-prepared batch.
The official menu says listed prices exclude VAT.
decemberNotes: December is a popular Chiang Mai travel month, so book ahead for a larger group and verify both holiday hours and dish availability. No 2026 seasonal event or dish-specific schedule was confirmed.
uncertainties: December 2026 menu prices, opening hours and availability may change; check directly shortly before visiting.
The venue does not publish step-free access or detailed allergen controls.
Transit fares and travel time vary; no fixed estimate is reliable without a starting point.
A common version contains pork, but recipes and condiments vary; do not assume the dish can be made vegetarian or allergen-safe.
